title: Check: Ordering and Total Order Broadcast

options: Every event has a wall-clock time
If A caused B, everyone sees A before B

questions.prompt: What does a Lamport timestamp attach to each operation?
options: A counter and the node id

questions.prompt: A node receives a message with counter 42 while its own counter is 7. What does it do?
Why can't Lamport timestamps alone enforce a unique username right now?
options: The order is only known after the fact; another node might claim it with a lower timestamp

questions.prompt: What two properties does total order broadcast guarantee?
options: Reliable delivery and the same order everywhere

questions.prompt: Feeding every replica the same writes in the same order so they end up in the same state is state ______ replication. (one word)
Total order broadcast is equivalent to consensus.
